These recommendations remain subject to each card's target and timing conditions. The [https://web.archive.org/web/20260422134639/https://res.starwarsccg.org/rules/SWCCG_2023_AdvancedRulebook.pdf 2023 Advanced Rulebook], p. 174, permits Effects on an undercover spy and, except during battle, permits Interrupts and cards targeting spies to target it. This supports Program Trap deployment, Nevar Yalnal when both players have a spy at the site, and E Chu Ta's protocol-droid insult outside battle; it does not assert that E Chu Ta's separate battle-initiation function uses an inactive undercover droid. The original U-3PO is a protocol droid and undercover spy. Page 155 separately confirms his power contribution without participation and Light's option to decline stealing him when cover breaks. The data record labels its 2023 wording revision a clarification with no gameplay change, not original printed wording. Preserved data copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261020183206/https://raw.githubusercontent.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/d4e661ec735dcb111266fbda98704f2181e1cfab/Dark.json Internet Archive] (20 October 2026). '''Virtual Legacy''' — [[Wampa (V)]] (1220_21) |sources=* [https://web.archive.org/web/20081225225012/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/index.html Star Wars CCG cardlists index] at Decipher.com (archive, 25 December 2008) * [https://web.archive.org/web/20070928014432/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/swallcards.pdf Complete Card List] (Decipher PDF, archive 28 September 2007) — Dark Creature: Wampa, Hoth, R2 |strategy=By Jim Van Fleet (RED 15)https://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/hoth/dark/small/wampa.html The most powerful creature card to date in the Decipher Star Wars Universe is the [[Wampa]], and he remains a favorite with Dark Side players who favor [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] as their stomping grounds. For those who play the increasingly popular [[Walker Garrison]] deck, a [[Wampa]] offers some unique advantages. If the Dark Side has a [[Hoth: Wampa Cave (7th Marker){{!}}Hoth: Wampa Cave]] on the table, they can deploy this creature for free. If there are any non-droid characters elsewhere on [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]], the [[Wampa]] begins to move towards them. Dark Side characters can avoid the [[Wampa]] (and Ice Storms, and blasters, lightsabers and etc.) by staying in Imperial Walkers or Blizzard Walkers. Light Side characters may be more vulnerable to attack, even if they are at interior sites. The [[Wampa]] is full of surprises, and packs a powerful punch, as [[Commander Luke Skywalker]] discovered. A Dark Side player could arrange a destiny draw of 7, making this creature a hard-to-beat 10 power in an attack! Wampas can deploy under the [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] shields, at locations without presence or even Force icons, wreaking havoc on an [[Echo Base Operations]] deck or a [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] numbers deck if it uses non-droid characters such as [[Wioslea]]! Finally, the [[Wampa]] has a unique ability: he may choose to send his victims to the [[Hoth: Wampa Cave (7th Marker){{!}}Hoth: Wampa Cave]] instead of the lost pile. Imagine a [[Wampa]] tearing through the [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]]: Echo Base Command Center, sending Light Side characters to the Cave one at a time, while the Dark Side sets up a welcoming committee of powerful characters in the Cave, guarded by Walkers with AT-AT Cannons at the exterior site just outside. Combo: , then a massive deployment to the [[Wampa]] Cave: Lots of punishment for the Light Side player, who can't move away, since his feet seem to have frozen into the ice! |combos=* [[Wampa]] + [[Cold Feet]][https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=Wampa Scomp: Wampa]; card data [https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json swccg-card-json Light.json] (commit d4e661ec). {{Set infobox |name=Premiere (Japanese) |image=Premiere-Japanese-box.png |publisher=[[Decipher]] / [[Takara]] |era=[[:Category:Decipher sets|Decipher]] (1995–2001) |released=April 1997 |cards=324 (162 Light, 162 Dark) |code=GEMP set 1301 |country=Japan |language=Japanese |next=[[A New Hope (Japanese)]] |related=[[Premiere Limited]] · [[Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game]] }} '''Premiere (Japanese)''' (基本カード) is the Japanese-language edition of [[Premiere Limited]]. [[Takara]] published it in Japan in April 1997 as スターウォーズコレクションカードゲーム. It has 324 black-border cards, 162 Light Side and 162 Dark Side, 108 of each rarity. Decipher and Takara announced the partnership in December 1996. Steve Stanley, Decipher Senior Vice President and General Counsel, visited Tokyo for Takara's introduction of the set. Takara demonstrated it at the Tokyo Toy Show, 19–23 March 1997, at Tokyo Big Sight. The first three days were trade only. The last two days were open to the public. Takara's gameplay demonstrations had standing room only. Hirohisa Satoh, Jr., President of Takara Ltd., hosted the display. Takara pre-sold more than 80 percent of the print run before street date. Takara was translating the Tournament Kit. Japan was placed in the newly created Ord Mantell region on Decipher's tournament locator. A Japanese champion was expected to compete at the [[1997 Decipher World Championship]]. Takara could not ship the Japanese cards outside Japan. The English Limited set is the 1st expansion of Star Wars CCG. This printing translates that 324-card pool. GEMP loads the Japanese faces as set 1301. English-language packs from [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] through [[Endor]] were sold in Japan with a Takara overlabel on the pack. Poor translations led Japanese players to prefer the English-language cards. Takara and Decipher ended the partnership after Japanese Premiere, [[A New Hope (Japanese)|A New Hope]], [[Hoth (Japanese)|Hoth]], and the two Japanese two-player games. [[Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game]] has a separate Japanese product. Language editions are listed on [[Translations of SWCCG]]. == Packaging == Takara sold 15-card booster packs (MSRP ¥500) in 36-pack boxes. Each pack had 10 commons, 4 uncommons and 1 rare. 60-card starters (MSRP ¥1400) came in 12-deck displays. Each starter had 44 commons (22 per side), 14 uncommons (7 per side), 2 rares (1 per side) and a Japanese rulebook. {| class="wikitable" style="background:transparent; border:none;" |- style="background:transparent; border:none; vertical-align:bottom;" | style="border:none; text-align:center;" | [[File:Premiere-Japanese-box.png|260px|Japanese booster box]]

If the Dark Side has a [[Hoth: Wampa Cave (7th Marker){{!}}Hoth: Wampa Cave]] on the table, they can deploy this creature for free. If there are any non-droid characters elsewhere on [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]], the [[Wampa]] begins to move towards them. Dark Side characters can avoid the [[Wampa]] (and Ice Storms, and blasters, lightsabers and etc.) by staying in Imperial Walkers or Blizzard Walkers. A Dark Side player could arrange a destiny draw of 7, making this creature a hard-to-beat 10 power in an attack! Wampas can deploy under the [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] shields, at locations without presence or even Force icons, wreaking havoc on an [[Echo Base Operations]] deck or a [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] numbers deck if it uses non-droid characters such as [[Wioslea]]! Imagine a [[Wampa]] tearing through the [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]]: Echo Base Command Center, sending Light Side characters to the Cave one at a time, while the Dark Side sets up a welcoming committee of powerful characters in the Cave, guarded by Walkers with AT-AT Cannons at the exterior site just outside.
